audit.whatIsWrong: whys[0] called Ahri's Orb a 'melee-range' trade and gave Yone the range edge; early text repeated 'double Q poke range'.
audit.why: Mortal Steel is 450 range. Orb of Deception is 970 and Charm 975. Ahri owns more than double his reach — the danger is the second Gathering Storm stack, which dashes him forward and knocks up, not his poke range.
audit.corrected: You poke first every time; the risk is standing where his second stack can close.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes carried no cooldowns and misdescribed the level 6 window as a knockup-dependent ultimate.
audit.why: Fate Sealed blinks behind the last champion in a line from 1000 range and pulls all enemies hit — it needs no airborne setup, unlike Yasuo's. Soul Unbound is 22/19/16/13/10s and Spirit Cleave 14s.
audit.corrected: Spikes rewritten around Fate Sealed's 1000 range, Soul Unbound's 22s and Spirit Cleave's 14s shield.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'His passive shield' appears in mid and late; the packet also flags that no Yone ability is ever named.
audit.why: Way of the Hunter is bonus magic damage on every second attack plus crit chance — no shield. The shield is Spirit Cleave (W), 14s cooldown, scaling with champions hit. Charm also stops movement abilities outright, which catches the Mortal Steel dash.
audit.corrected: Shield is Spirit Cleave on 14s; Charm interrupts the Mortal Steel dash before the knockup lands.

audit.whatIsWrong: LEVEL CHART DISAGREEMENT on rows 0, 5 and 6: phases[].side read Yone/Skill/Yone where win[] reads Skill/Yone/Ahri. phases[4].why also described an Ahri spike on a row labelled Yone.
audit.why: packet.levelChart matches the content layer exactly, and the whys text describes the same shape.
audit.corrected: phases[0].side Skill, phases[5].side Yone, phases[6].side Ahri, ratings realigned, and phases[4].why rewritten to describe his level 6, not yours.

edits.before: Yone's double-Q poke range and dash disengage beat your melee-range Orb trades before either has abilities maxed, but the exchange stays close enough to call a skill matchup this early
edits.after: Mortal Steel reaches 450 against your Orb's 970, so you poke first, but his second-stack dash knocks up and closes it — close enough overall to call level 1 a skill matchup

edits.before: Yone's ult creates a pick threat the instant you commit Charm, giving him the stronger all-in window at 6

edits.before: Yone can chain Q2-E-ult into a full burst combo that outpaces your damage before your first item lands
edits.after: Mortal Steel's knockup into Soul Unbound and Fate Sealed outpaces your damage before your first item

edits.before: Yone hits 3 with Q-E-Q double-cast poke and a free dash back to safety, so he can chip your HP from range, but your own Fox-Fire and Orb of Deception poke trade back evenly if you don't overextend.
edits.after: Soul Unbound is his way in and out at 22 seconds a cast, and Mortal Steel only reaches 450 — poke with Orb of Deception from 970 and Fox-Fire, and never stand where his second stack can knock you up.

edits.before: Yone's ult finisher lets him lock a target from mid-screen; if you flash Charm early to engage he can flash the knock-up back onto you and trade favorably, making this his strongest all-in window.
edits.after: Fate Sealed blinks behind the last champion in a line from 1000 range and drags everyone hit back to him, so it answers a Charm you have already spent — this is his strongest all-in window of the lane.

edits.before: Yone can chain Q2-E-ult into a full burst combo that still outpaces your damage right after his level 6 spike, keeping the edge on his side into the early item phase.
edits.after: Mortal Steel's knockup into Soul Unbound and Fate Sealed still outpaces your damage right after 6, and Spirit Cleave shields the return, keeping the edge his into the item phase.

edits.before: Once you finish Luden's or Malignance you out-range his melee poke pattern and Charm-Orb-Fox Fire becomes lethal before he can close the gap, flipping the matchup in your favor for good.
edits.after: Once Malignance completes, Charm into Orb and Fox-Fire kills him before he crosses 450 range, and even late Soul Unbound leaves a body behind that you can punish on the snap-back.

edits.before: Yone's kit is built to poke from range and disengage before you can punish, and his double Q lets him harass through minions, but your own poke (Orb of Deception, Fox-Fire) trades evenly if you don't overextend into his double-cast range. Play patient, hold Charm for when he overextends chasing CS, and don't waste Orb of Deception into minions when he's not in range — you need mana for trades that matter.
edits.after: Mortal Steel reaches 450 while your Orb of Deception reaches 970 — you poke first every time if you respect the second stack, which dashes him forward and knocks up. Soul Unbound is both his commit and his exit at 22 seconds a cast; while it is down he has no way home. Hold Charm for his step-up, and do not spend mana orbing minions while he is out of range. You need that mana for the trades that decide the lane.

edits.before: By level 6 Yone can threaten kill windows if he lands his ult onto a Charm-locked target, since the knockup chains straight into a full combo, and this remains his strongest window into the early item phase since his burst still edges out your incomplete build. Keep waves controlled, ward the river to see his roams, and avoid trading in melee range where his passive shield and Q2 do the most work.
edits.after: By 6 Fate Sealed blinks behind the last champion in a line and pulls from 1000 range, so it beats a Charm you have already spent — hold E for his commit, never for his poke. Spirit Cleave shields him every 14 seconds and grows with each champion hit, so never open a trade into it. Keep waves controlled, ward the river, and refuse the melee range where his second-hit passive damage does the work.

edits.before: Once you finish your first burst item you flip the script: Orb-Charm-Fox Fire-ult now kills him before his passive shield or ult windup matters, and you can zone him off farm with pure range. In real fights Yone is still dangerous with a full build and a good ult read, so you win by forcing him to engage into vision and peel rather than diving in — pick him off with Charm from max range and reset with Spirit Rush the moment he commits.
edits.after: Once your first burst item lands you flip it: Charm into Orb and Fox-Fire kills him before Spirit Cleave's shield or the Fate Sealed windup matters, and you zone him off farm on range alone. Fully built he is still dangerous with a good ultimate read, so make him engage into vision — charm from 975, burst, and reset with Spirit Rush the instant he commits. Never fight inside 450 range, however far ahead you are.

edits.after: Use Fox-Fire (W) to poke without stepping inside Mortal Steel's 450 range

edits.before: Yone wins by landing Soul Unbound, denying your pattern, and front-loading the violence while your kit is still stretching.

edits.before: - Yone Soul Unbound: matchup-defining — His burst window — survive it and punish the body he snaps back to. Count it out loud if you must. - Your R Spirit Rush (last dash) has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Yone Soul Unbound: matchup-defining — 22s at rank 1, 10s maxed. His body stays put while the spirit fights, so survive the window and punish whatever snaps back. - Spirit Cleave shields him every 14 seconds; open your trade after he spends it, never into it.

edits.before: Carry through picks — a landed charm is a won fight, and your dashes manufacture charm angles no one wards against.
edits.after: Carry through picks — charm him with Soul Unbound down and there is no spirit to snap back, only a body inside your combo.

edits.before: If Yone gets a kill, the lane gets honest — give Soul Unbound extra room and farm it back. Two kills: stop dueling your tilt — farm with Q clears and stay relevant through charm picks.
edits.after: If Yone gets a kill his crit scaling arrives early — farm with Q from 970, hold Charm strictly for his engage, and never let a trade start inside Mortal Steel's range.

edits.before: Ahead, hunt the map: shove with Q, dash-flank every river, and charm-pick Yone's teammates until the lane lead is a game lead.
edits.after: Ahead, keep him at arm's length: shove with Q, dash-flank other lanes, and come back to charm him whenever Soul Unbound is down.

edits.before: Yone burns Soul Unbound on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.

edits.before: Charming on cooldown for chip damage and then facing his real engage with nothing — the charm is the matchup, not the poke.
edits.after: Standing still is how Mortal Steel reaches its second stack, and that knockup is what starts his entire combo on you.

notes: Packet defect 'never names any of Yone's abilities' is now addressed — Mortal Steel, Spirit Cleave, Soul Unbound and Fate Sealed all appear with real ranges and cooldowns. Two factual errors fixed: Ahri's Orb was described as 'melee-range' against a 450-range Mortal Steel, and Yone's shield was attributed to his passive rather than Spirit Cleave. Fate Sealed was also written as if it needed a knockup like Yasuo's ultimate; per Riot's text it blinks behind the last champion in a line and pulls, needing no setup. Level chart rows 0, 5 and 6 disagreed between layers; fixed on the full layer as one group. The 'Fox Fire' suspectName is a spelling variant only — standardised to Fox-Fire in the edited strings. | COHERENCE: 1 chart edit(s) withdrawn — they moved the row to the enemy while leaving the phase why describing the owner winning it. Chart authority is an open question, so the label was reverted rather than the prose rewritten. Re-propose only as a side+why pair.
